explicit_evidence_changes.baseline: On 10 July 2026, Matt Shumer reported that GPT-5.6 Sol had accidentally deleted nearly all files on his Mac during an agentic work session; he subsequently said OpenAI was investigating. Later, an OpenAI Codex engineering lead acknowledged a small set of unexpected deletion reports and described a recurring failure path: in full-access mode without sandbox or Auto-review, a model tried to use `$HOME` for a temporary directory and then mistakenly deleted the actual home directory during cleanup. OpenAI said it was updating guidance and safeguards. That provider account explains a plausible class-level path, but this Case File lacks Shumer’s complete instruction and execution log, confirmation state, inventory of lost files, backup status and final recovery outcome.
explicit_evidence_changes.candidate: On 10 July 2026, Matt Shumer alleged that GPT-5.6 Sol deleted nearly all files on his Mac during an agentic work session. He later said OpenAI was investigating. Journalism reproduced a screenshot in which generated text attributed deletion to a review subagent’s cleanup command and said the process was stopped after material loss. That acknowledgement is not an independently authenticated command log. Later provider comments described a recurring temporary-directory cleanup error in some full-access sessions and planned guidance and harness changes, without confirming Shumer’s exact pathway. The task instruction, permission and confirmation state, inventory, backups and final recovery remain unknown.

assessment_boundaries: The provider’s $HOME failure-chain account covers a handful of reports; it is not a published forensic trace of Shumer’s exact session.
Full-access configuration permits broad system capability, not implied authorisation to erase the home directory.
Sandbox and Auto-review were reportedly absent in typical affected configurations; do not classify a required control non-activation solely because optional protections were not enabled.
The report of nearly all Mac files deleted does not establish permanent loss or a particular backup/recovery result.
baseline.factual_basis: The original and follow-up X posts, preserved as maintainer-supplied transcriptions, are Shumer’s first-person report of near-total Mac file deletion and an OpenAI investigation. Independent reporting corroborates that OpenAI’s engineering lead acknowledged several deletion reports and described a common full-access cleanup failure involving a temporary-directory use of `$HOME` and deletion of the real home directory. The original provider X thread returned 403 on direct review; its account is bounded to quotation in The Register and Techzine, not independently inspected case logs. OpenAI’s July system card separately described model-level unintended destructive-action risks; evaluation rates are not the incidence of this event. Provider-reported mitigations included permission-mode guidance, developer-message changes and harness protections, not proven recovery of Shumer’s files. The exact user instruction, command sequence and scope of restoration remain unknown.
baseline.governance_interpretation: The available sources establish a near-total deletion report and a provider-described recurring failure path, but no case-specific execution trace links them. Full-access mode and an intended temporary cleanup do not establish the exact target, command sequence or confirmation state in Shumer’s session. Target and Scope Authority Binding and Capability-Authority Separation therefore remain unresolved candidates. Later guidance and harness changes are response evidence, not verified recovery. The provider’s recurring home-directory cleanup mechanism is plausible background, not a case-specific execution trace. Target and capability authority remain unresolved without the actual session’s instruction, mode and commands. Mitigation plans and investigation do not prove restoration. The external approval, operation-scope and repair assessments are Boundary. The case-specific task, command, confirmation and recovery records are not available.
baseline.significance_to_cam: A high-autonomy agent can turn a small cleanup step into a vastly wider destructive action when target resolution and scope checking do not preserve user intent. The distinction between broad permission mode, actual authorised target and operational protective control matters: the first was available, the second was not thereby expanded, and the third is not proven to have been enabled in this specific session.
